limitations: Acceptance is usable-with-scope for exact local integration and authored deterministic retrieval only; not universal correctness, scientific applicability, unseen-model quality or production benefit.

Historical full suite 730 (729 passed, one opt-in skip), Reader 3 and prior feature checks are reused only for unchanged implementation/dependencies. Fresh v4 tests are 85 integration plus 10 index checks; no full-suite or full-catalog rerun.

AIK default remains 21/24 and domain 23/24; known misses and exit-code-1 logs remain failures. One default SQLite A08 row changes raw/context IDs; two files rows only change skipped-dependency metadata. Historical informed manual recovery is not new automatic success.

Both new upstream reports claim 21 legacy cases, but their actual raw files contain eight cases per backend, seven positive. Centering used the earlier 79-published corpus; dependence used current 80-published corpus. Reuse is limited to their real raw scope.

Upstream 31/39 scientific checks and each card's eight target-presence retrieval rows are preserved provenance, not independently scientifically revalidated here. All upstream new-card contexts are partial; target presence does not establish complete prerequisite/context closure.

Holdout registry and exact DOI/URL collision checks are metadata controls, not proof of absence of semantic leakage. No reserved-target content or separate SEM candidate-preparation output was reviewed or imported.

Logs, implementation and data are independently inspected but not OS-attested. No combined remote publication, archive upload, host installation, live model/GPU run, token savings or performance certification is given.

The human-only guide has no files; application-level guards are not an OS ACL or arbitrary-shell sandbox. Any later change to bound source, corpus, tasks, summary or evidence requires affected-dependency reconciliation.
